pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Free ACL RX fragments on disconnection
pr_body:
This function call frees the buffer kept by the host for reassembling L2CAP
PDUs into.

Without this call, the current buffer will eventually be
leaked, leading to a non-functional host due to lack of RX buffers.

The effect is worse when host flow control is not enabled, as the RX
buffer pool is shared with events, which means communication with the
controller is essentially dead.

Fixes #76781
pr_comments: @jori-nordic shouldn't this also be marked as fixing #76737?

No, I messed up when I tagged the issue initially.
The fix for TX is still being worked on (the test rather). I'll submit it next week.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Deadlock because of Missing L2CAP RX reassembly state cleanup on disconnect
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When reconnecting a Bluetooth connection, a deadlock may occur when the host issues an HCI command.
This occurs after that a link was disconnected before it received all L2CAP fragments of an L2CAP PDU.


**To Reproduce**
* Run a connection with a long connection interval.
* Set max data length to 27 bytes.
* Send long ATT/L2CAP packets
* Disconnect one of the devices
* Reconnect. Observe that the `bt_hci_cmd_send_sync()` triggers an HCI command timeout.


Calling `bt_conn_reset_rx_state(conn);` in `bt_conn_set_state()` when the old state is `BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE` and the new state is `BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED` resolves the issue.

**Expected behavior**
Upon disconnection all previous state shall be cleared.

**Impact**
Showstopper

**Logs and console output**
Logs extracted from a custom test
```
connected: err 0 addr F6:A4:15:3B:7A:F7 (random)
disconnected: err 16 addr F6:A4:15:3B:7A:F7 (random)
connected: err 0 addr F6:A4:15:3B:7A:F7 (random)
disconnected: err 16 addr F6:A4:15:3B:7A:F7 (random)
connected: err 0 addr F6:A4:15:3B:7A:F7 (random)
ASSERTION FAIL [err == 0] @ WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c:411
  Controller unresponsive, command opcode 0x2016 timeout with err -11
  @ WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c:411
  os: >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 3: Kernel oops on CPU 0
  os: Current thread: 0x8146760 (BT RX WQ)
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Zephyr 3.7.0

**Additional context**
The bug was introduced in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/72090

review_comments: We should assert that `rp->le_max_len` is large enough to send a long l2cap packet. The other option is to rely on that the controller supports this length and validates when it receives it. If we do that we do not have to issue `BT_HCI_OP_LE_READ_BUFFER_SIZE`
what do you mean by long l2cap packet? isn't it decoupled from controller buffer size?
I meant that the buffer size is large enough to fit an L2CAP packet in a single HCI Data packet right
We should validate the content of the notification we got.

should we? I guess I can, it makes the test stricter. 
The purpose was just checking for leaks though.
I have no strong opinion here. I just though it made sense to add some simple, cheap validation here.

It looks like we are not doing anything with incoming data other than setting `flag_write_ack`. Is there something I've missed? If we are not using it, I would consider removing all the related code to simplify the test
Useful for debugging (ie if the remote starts sending unexpected ATT messages). I'll keep it.
Why do we both give and take the `cmd_sem` here?

had to scratch my head a bit haha. I'm re-using `cmd_sem` as a signal that we are able to send another command, which means that the current command (for which we took `cmd_sem` above) likely has gotten a response. 
We don't actually want to send anything more, so when we got that signal (ie the thread is un-suspended), then we release the sem immediately.
Maybe add some docs here to explain that?

Where does the `on_air` value 5 come from? 
I would prefer that NOTIFICATION_PAYLOAD is longer than 27 bytes to guarantee that the controller cannot send the data in a single packet as some implementations may choose to buffer payload until nothing more can fit.
I was doing that to avoid having to do a GATT MTU exchange. I agree that it depends on the controller impl.
You may consider leaving out the command setting the event mask. The controller is already initialized with a default event mast

FYI @cvinayak , the spec states:
> The value with all bits set to 0 indicates that no events are specified. The
default is for bits 0 to 4 (the value 0x0000 0000 0000 001F) to be set.
